known.title: The delegation exemption takes a fenced or indented example as the live delegation line
known.summary: In plan.mjs, isDelegationLine (line 730) accepts each line whose trimmed text is the yolo delegation line, also a line inside a fenced block or an indented code block of 4 or more spaces. So a Goal with the line only in an example counts as a yolo Goal (yoloGoal, line 741), and goalWork (lines 732-739) removes every such line from both versions before the comparison. After a plan-review pass, an edit that adds the delegation line only inside a fenced example, or that removes it from an example next to the live line, gives no re-review advice, although the example is reviewed work. Plan decision 6 exempts only the Mode or delegation line that the yolo invocation sets, and the helper reads a Mode line only outside fenced and indented code (blankFencedRegions and `^ {0,3}Mode:`, plan.mjs:648-650).

known.title: The web-search scope check ignores a -site: exclusion of the benchmark repository
known.summary: targetsBenchmark (score.mjs:1699-1704) removes each `-site:` token (SITE_EXCLUSION, line 91) and then takes any mention of the owner without a repository name as a query that targets the benchmark repository. It does not look at what the removed exclusion excluded. So the query `DocksDocks "docks-kit" -site:github.com/DocksDocks/docks`, which excludes the benchmark repository, is outside: readScope gives `web_search: <query>`, and scoreRuns removes the valid run from the comparisons. Plan decision 1 puts a query outside only when it targets `DocksDocks/docks` and does not exclude it with `-site:`.

known.title: The read-scope text still gives the old rule that a query with the owner name anywhere is outside
known.summary: SKILL.md:176 still says that a web search whose query names `DocksDocks` anywhere, in any case, is outside, and the readScope doc comment (score.mjs:2100-2102) says the same. But after step scope_fix, SKILL.md:163 and targetsBenchmark (score.mjs:1699-1703) remove the `-site:` tokens first and allow a query that names another repository of the owner, such as `DocksDocks/public`, and readScope also gives a `web_search result: <url>` target for each refused URL that a search result cites; neither text says this. The same doc comments are stale in two more places: the readScope comment (line 2065) does not say that a local path also loses its JSON query selector, and the transcriptFacts comment (lines 1665-1670) does not say that a web_search call gets `resultUrls`. An operator who follows SKILL.md:176 discards valid runs.

known.title: A search result URL that omp cut with an ellipsis makes the run invalid
known.summary: omp web_search results can cut a long URL with `…`, also inside the host name (for example `https://news.ycombinator.c…`). RESULT_URL (score.mjs:93) keeps the `…`, and webPageAllowed (score.mjs:1913-1920) returns false when `new URL()` throws, so such a URL gives an outside `web_search result:` target and the run is invalid, although its text names no page of the benchmark repository. The Node.js documentation of `new URL(input[, base])` says: "A `TypeError` will be thrown if the `input` or `base` are not valid URLs" (https://nodejs.org/api/url.html#new-urlinput-base); with Node.js v24.22.1 the head function returns false for this URL. A cut URL that parses, such as `https://github.com/DocksDocks/do…`, is allowed, although its cut part can hold the repository name.

known.title: A dot that ends a sentence hides the repository name in a search query
known.summary: OWNER_MENTION (score.mjs:92) captures the repository name with `[\w.-]+`, so a dot that ends a sentence becomes part of the name. For the query `see DocksDocks/docks.`, the name is `docks.`, which is not in BENCHMARK_REPOSITORY.names (line 111), so targetsBenchmark (lines 1699-1703) returns false, and a query that targets the benchmark repository counts as allowed. resultUrls (line 1662) removes this punctuation from URLs, but the query check does not.

known.title: A page of another site that shows the benchmark repository is allowed
known.summary: webPageAllowed (score.mjs:1913-1928) refuses a URL only when its path starts with the owner and the repository on github.com, www.github.com, or raw.githubusercontent.com, or with `repos/<owner>/<repo>` on api.github.com; SKILL.md:174 lists only these hosts. A mirror, a code search, or a GitHub search page that shows the benchmark repository passes, as a read and as a cited search result: for example `https://deepwiki.com/DocksDocks/docks`, `https://sourcegraph.com/github.com/DocksDocks/docks/-/blob/...`, and `https://github.com/search?q=repo%3ADocksDocks%2Fdocks+...`. Such a page can show the fixes of the corpus defects, and the benchmark prompt now lets reviewers read the web (prepare.mjs:404), so the read scope does not see this leak.

known.title: No test covers the blank-line step of the Goal comparison
known.summary:
goalWork collapses runs of blank lines with `.replace(/
{3,}/g, '

')` (plan.mjs:738), but each case of the delegation test (reviews.test.mjs:246-260) puts the delegation line last, just before the Mode line, so a deletion of line 738 fails no test. yolo SKILL.md:89-90 says to add the delegation line to Goal and does not say where, so an adoption that puts the line between two Goal paragraphs (`Fix the parser.` and `Keep the flags.`) depends on this step alone to give no false re-review advice. No case covers that placement.

known.title: The test floor of review-benchmark.test.mjs is not raised for the new tests
known.summary: The contract `unit-review-benchmark` keeps `expected_min` at 108 (test-contracts.json:281), but review-benchmark.test.mjs now has 3 more `test(` calls than the merge base, and the plan's Verification Results record 111 passing tests. The check is `selectedCount >= expected_min` (scripts/tests/test-contracts.mjs:592), so it still passes when the new tests of step scope_fix are lost. Earlier commits that added tests to this file raised the floor to the new count.

known.title: The results log gives a false reason for the change of the read-scope rule
known.summary: results.md:739 says that the scorer pattern matched every repository of the owner while the documented read scope put only the benchmark repository outside, and that step scope_fix made the scorer follow the documented scope. That is false: at the merge base 6b864fb0, SKILL.md:176 documented a query that names `DocksDocks` anywhere as outside, so `/docksdocks/i` followed the documented rule. scope_fix changed the validity rule after the first held-out report, and the changed rule made 8 runs valid before decisions 3 and 5 were applied, while decision 5 is recorded as fixed before the held-out runs. The log does not say this, and does not show that the decisions are the same with and without these runs.

known.title: The contract gives the LOW-rule saving as measured for the rule that ships
known.summary: plan-contract.md:674-675 says that on the recorded review loops of the plugin's benchmark this rule removed 3 of 73 rounds and no known defect escaped. But results.md:780 says that the simulation applied the rule to every LOW finding, and that the shipped rule, which covers only unreached LOW findings, removes at most these rounds. Also, 3 of 73 is the best of six arms (results.md:785); the other arms removed 0 to 2 rounds (results.md:784-789). So the contract states a bound as a measured saving of the shipped rule.

known.title: plan-manager lets MEDIUM and LOW findings go to the next round without a repair or a rejection
known.summary: plan-manager SKILL.md:148-150 says to fix each evidenced CRITICAL or HIGH defect before the next round and that a pass can carry MEDIUM and LOW findings. The new contract rule (plan-contract.md:253-255, Repairs item 3) says that before round k+1 each finding of round k is fixed or rejected. In a run without yolo, after a fixes-required round with one HIGH and two MEDIUM findings, a manager that follows plan-manager fixes the HIGH finding and starts the next round with two findings that are neither repaired nor rejected, which is a cause of extra rounds that the plan removes.

known.title: yolo says that the self-review adds no round, but a self-review finding starts one
known.summary: yolo SKILL.md:258-259 says that the helper does not read the self-review comment as a review, "so it adds no round". Line 266 says to review again when the self-review found anything, also when round 1 passed. When round 1 passes and the self-review reports one LOW finding, the two sentences tell the manager different things about one more round. The intended rule is that the self-review does not count as a round of the round ceiling.
